clue.text: Guidance shown by religious clique over time

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit over, above, the last one

parts.note: PI is a crossword abbreviation for pious, so religious
a lot is a set or group of people, a clique
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A religious sect has offered guidance over many years.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilotage is the act of steering a ship, so direction or guidance.

parts.note: kin are one's relatives, a family group

explanation.surface: Two things compared are as alike as members of one family.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin to means related or of like kind, so similar to something.

clue.text: Record jazz session — end in deadlock!

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
a jam is an informal improvised jazz session

explanation.surface: A recorded jazz session ends with the musicians at a stalemate.
explanation.definitionFit: A logjam is a blockage of floating logs, figuratively a deadlock or impasse.

parts.note: reads as being far from shore, but describes someone feeling ill while out at sea

explanation.surface: Someone is not far enough away from the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not well away' looks like 'not far away'; parse it instead as 'unwell, away from land'.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling nauseous on board ship, out of sight of land, is the familiar ailment of sailors.

indicators.note: a kind of leaf suggests a variety of the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder; that the insect also runs on inside 'of leaf' is a coincidence, as 'Kind of' signals rearrangement

explanation.surface: A naturalist identifies an insect that resembles a leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a small jumping parasitic insect.

parts.note: suggests a touching stage entry, but means a castle's gateway bridge that is raised and lowered

explanation.surface: An actor makes an emotional, affecting first appearance on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' means stirring emotions in the surface, but literally it is an entrance that physically moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged bridge over a moat, raised to bar access, is a castle entrance that literally moves.

clue.text: A scoundrel who deserves no good fortune

parts.note: bad means no good, worthless
one's lot is one's fortune or destiny

explanation.surface: A rogue gets no luck because he does not deserve any.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad lot is an idiom for a dishonest or worthless person, a rogue.

clue.text: Giving reason for absence, ticks one off

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or wrong tells us these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A teacher ticks off one pupil who arrives with an excuse for missing class.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a doctor's certificate is the thing giving reason for an absence from work.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's certificate excusing an employee from work explains why they are away.

clue.text: Grub right at the centre of a burning issue

indicators.note: one letter is placed in the middle of the following phrase

parts.note: lava is molten rock that issues from a volcano, literally a burning issue

explanation.surface: The grub, an insect, lies at the heart of a hot controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A burning issue' looks like a hot topic but is read literally as molten outpouring.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the larval stage of an insect, as of a beetle.

parts.note: many birds, and many pillows, have the fine fluffy plumage meant here

explanation.surface: Lots of creatures are covered in fluffy plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine soft under-plumage of birds, used to stuff quilts, is what is described.

clue.text: The sea seems quite calm, fortunately

definitions.meaning: read as three words: only a gentle rolling wave, nothing rough
meaning luckily or it is as well that it is so

explanation.walkthrough: Split the phrase as JUST A SWELL for the sea reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means it is fortunate or no bad thing; split, it describes merely a gentle swell at sea.

parts.note: suggests generous with cash, but means to release a captive by paying

explanation.surface: Someone spends generously and lavishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free with money' looks like generous; read 'free' as a verb, to liberate by payment.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a hostage in exchange for a payment is exactly this verb.

clue.text: This takes its time, making one late

definitions.text: This takes its time, making one late

parts.words: This takes its time, making one late
parts.note: late here means dead, so something that acts gradually and kills

explanation.surface: Something that dawdles makes a person behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' looks like tardy but is the sense deceased, as in the late king.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxin that acts gradually over time eventually kills, making the victim the late so-and-so.

indicators.note: the small word is put inside the vegetable here

parts.note: celery is a plant grown as a vegetable

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get that seedling in the ground quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a formal word for swiftness or speed.
The word means both to recline flat and a falsehood.

definitions.meaning: further portions of food after the first
a boxer's or duellist's assistants, who help at the fight

explanation.definitionFit: Second portions of a meal, and the attendants who assist a boxer or duellist.

indicators.note: not quite the full word means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: done means finished or completed

explanation.surface: Someone suspects the work is incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothing is to put it on, as one assumes a garment or disguise.

parts.note: the head is the principal of a school
a way is a method or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: A headteacher describes the main means of advancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To make headway is to advance or progress, especially against difficulty.

parts.note: suggests people having fun, but means the spectators at a theatrical performance

explanation.surface: People are relaxing and having fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At play' looks like playing; read it as attending a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: The spectators watching a stage performance are collectively its listeners and viewers.

parts.note: suggests a bird, but wings are the stage sides and flies the space above the stage

explanation.surface: Something winged that takes to the air, like a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Wings and flies are stage terms: the side areas and the loft where scenery hangs.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse has offstage wings at the sides and a fly tower above the stage.

clue.text: When a girl may scream in case of necessity

definitions.meaning: when she is nipped or squeezed by someone's fingers

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means if really necessary, and literally describes being nipped.

indicators.note: accommodation suggests these letters are rearranged to fit, adapted

explanation.surface: A landlord advertises a rented flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accommodation' looks like housing but signals that RENTED is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender is to formally offer, as a resignation or a bid.

clue.text: Lapsed badly, but asks for mercy

indicators.note: badly means the letters of the word beside it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sinner who lapsed badly now begs forgiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to appeal earnestly, as one begging for mercy does.

clue.text: It's not really used as a prefix

definitions.text: It's not really used as a prefix

parts.words: It's not really used as a prefix
parts.note: describes a combining form meaning false or sham, attached at the front of words

explanation.surface: A grammarian notes that a word is seldom put at the start of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not really' looks like 'seldom' but is what the form means: false or sham, as in a fake intellectual.
explanation.definitionFit: The combining form meaning false, as in fake-name words, is placed before other words.

clue.text: Ground speed of a slow-moving shell

definitions.text: Ground speed of a slow-moving shell

parts.words: Ground speed of a slow-moving shell
parts.note: ground speed suggests aircraft or artillery, but the shell is a mollusc's

explanation.surface: Artillery measures the velocity of a sluggish projectile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' suggests an artillery round; it is the mollusc carrying its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for an extremely slow rate, named after the slow mollusc.
The past tense of slay, and a verb meaning to turn or swivel suddenly.

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of US president Abraham Lincoln
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Was Lincoln dead or just asleep? It seemed so.
explanation.definitionFit: Abed is an old word for in bed, hence sleeping.

clue.text: Crooked king is in a bad way

indicators.note: the king is placed inside the following letters
bad here signals the letters of the word beside it are disordered

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A dishonest monarch finds himself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges WAY to AWY, and 'is in' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Awry means askew or not straight, so crooked.

clue.text: Run away to marry East European on the rebound

indicators.note: rebounding means bouncing back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A jilted man on the rebound runs off to wed an Eastern European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rebound' reverses E + POLE as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run off secretly in order to get married.

clue.text: Ruddy good fellow, but not Oxbridge material

parts.note: ruddy means reddish in colour
a brick is old slang for a reliable, good-hearted person

explanation.surface: A red-faced decent chap who is not Oxford or Cambridge calibre.
explanation.walkthrough: Red-brick universities are British civic universities founded in the Victorian era, contrasted with Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes British universities other than the ancient ones, built of brick rather than stone.
